title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 43 (Any one of joint promisors may be compelled to perform)

content.overview: Section 43 provides that when two or more persons make a joint promise, the promisee may, in the absence of express agreement to the contrary, compel any one or more of such joint promisors to perform the whole of the promise. Each of two or more joint promisors may compel every other joint promisor to contribute equally with himself to the performance of the promise, unless a contrary intention appears from the contract. If any one of two or more joint promisors makes default in such contribution, the remaining joint promisors must bear the loss arising from such default in equal shares.
content.glance: Promisee may compel any one joint promisor for the whole; joint promisors contribute equally inter se; default loss shared equally by remaining.
content.study: Absent express agreement to the contrary, the promisee may compel any one or more of the joint promisors to perform the whole promise. Inter se, each joint promisor may compel equal contribution unless contrary intention. Default in contribution: remaining joint promisors bear the loss in equal shares. Current-law framing: apply the promisee’s election against any joint promisor; then apply contribution and default-sharing rules among joint promisors.

sections.heading: Promisee may compel any one
sections.body: Promisee may compel any one or more of the joint promisors to perform the whole of the promise (absent express contrary agreement).

sections.heading: Equal contribution
sections.body: Each joint promisor may compel every other to contribute equally, unless contrary intention.

sections.heading: Default in contribution
sections.body: Remaining joint promisors bear the loss from default in equal shares.

provisions.title: Any one of joint promisors may be compelled to perform

examples.title: One of three compelled
examples.body: A, B and C jointly promise to pay D ₹3,000. D may compel A alone to pay the whole under s. 43. A may then claim contribution from B and C.

hypotheticals.question: Must the promisee sue all joint promisors together?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 43 allows the promisee to compel any one or more to perform the whole, absent express contrary agreement.

misconceptions.trap: The promisee can only recover a proportionate share from each joint promisor.
misconceptions.correction: Section 43 allows the promisee to compel any one for the whole; contribution is among the joint promisors inter se.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 43 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Apply promisee’s election against any joint promisor for the whole. II. Apply equal contribution inter se. III. Apply default-sharing. IV. Conclude.

examTips: State promisee’s right to compel any one for the whole.
